Split the conjunction into two independent analytic estimates.

Near \(s=1\), use the pole-removing factor
\[
g(s)=(s-1)\zeta(s).
\]
The standard continuation of \(\zeta\) gives \(g\) holomorphic near \(1\) with \(g(1)\neq0\). After shrinking to a neighborhood \(U\) where \(g\) has no zeros,
\[
-\frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)}-\frac1{s-1}
=-\frac{g'(s)}{g(s)}.
\]
The right-hand side is holomorphic, hence locally bounded; this yields the required `BddAbove` statement on \(U\setminus\{1\}\).

For the second conjunct, invoke a standard zero-counting estimate such as
\[
|N(T)|\le C\,T\log T \qquad (T\ge2).
\]
Then use \(\log T\le C' T^{1/2}\) on \([2,\infty)\), enlarge the constant if necessary, and obtain
\[
|N(T)|\le A T^{3/2}
\]
with \(A>0\). Finally combine the two witnesses.
